newsitem.title: USA: Sears says strong Q1 led by apparel sales.
newsitem.headline: Sears says strong Q1 led by apparel sales.

text.p: Sears Roebuck and Co said Thursday strong first-quarter results were led by solid sales increases in apparel lines, including women's sportswear and dresses, children's apparel and footwear.

Hardlines sales were led by lawn tractors and mowers, said the giant retailer, which reported first-quarter net income of $182 million on sales of $8.76 billion. Net income in the same period a year ago was $151 million on sales of $7.99 billion.
"We continue to drive revenue increases through our off-the-mall growth strategy," said Sears chairman and chief executive Arthur Martinez.
Sears has added more than 300 hardware, furniture, automotive and dealer stores since the first quarter last year, Martinez said.
"Total off-the-mall store revenues grew nearly 17 percent in the quarter, including double-digit same store sales increases in our hardware and dealer stores," he said.

First-quarter 1997 income from domestic operations increased 37.8 percent to $227 million, from $165 million a year before, Sears reported. The 1997 figure was boosted $38 million by an accounting change, the company added.
Revenues from domestic operations in the first quarter were $8 billion, a 9.8 percent increase over $7.29 billion in the 1996 period, Sears said.

Domestic gross margins as a percentage of merchandise sales and services in the first quarter increased to 24.6 percent from 24.4 percent a year ago. "Our gross margin rate continued to benefit from a shift in the balance of sales to higher-margin apparel merchandise," Martinez said.
Domestic operations selling and administrative expense as a percentage of revenues improved to 21.4 percent on the quarter from 21.8 percent a year earlier, Sears reported.

Depreciation expense for domestic operations increased $24 million, or 17 percent, to $165 million in the first quarter due primarily to modernizations and expansions of selling space in Sears stores, the company said.
Sears -- the second-largest U.S. retailer -- operates 823 full-line stores and more than 2,500 off-the-mall stores.
